title: 5. The Rescue of the Tin Woodman

paragraphs.en: Dorothy woke up to find Toto chasing birds. She noticed Scarecrow still standing patiently in his corner.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西醒来时发现托托在追逐小鸟。她注意到稻草人仍静静地站在自己的角落里，耐心地等待着。

paragraphs.en: "We must search for water," Dorothy said.
paragraphs.zh: “我们必须找水喝,”多萝西说道。

paragraphs.en: "Why do you need it?" asked Scarecrow thoughtfully.
paragraphs.zh: “你需要它做什么？”稻草人沉思着问道。

paragraphs.en: "To wash and drink, so I can eat without difficulty," she replied.
paragraphs.zh: “为了清洗并补充水分，这样我就能轻松进食了。”她回答道。

paragraphs.en: Scarecrow commented on the inconvenience of having flesh, but praised her brains. They left the cottage and found a spring where Dorothy drank, bathed, and ate breakfast. She noticed little bread was left in the basket.
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人抱怨起拥有肉体的不便，但称赞她的智慧。他们离开了小屋，在一个泉水边找到了多萝西喝水、洗澡和吃早餐的地方。她注意到篮子里剩下的面包不多了。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy heard a groan nearby and asked Scarecrow what it could be. They approached and saw a tin man behind them, motionless with an axe raised. Toto barked at his legs.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西听到附近传来一声呻吟，便问稻草人那声音是什么。他们走近一看，发现一个锡人站在他们身后，一动不动，手里还举着一把斧头。托托冲上前对着锡人的腿叫了起来。

paragraphs.en: "Did you groan?" Dorothy asked the tin man.
paragraphs.zh: “你呻吟了吗？”多萝西问那个铁皮人。

paragraphs.en: "Yes," he replied, explaining he had been groaning for over a year without help.
paragraphs.zh: “是的，”他回答道，“我已经疼了整整一年，一直没有人帮忙。”

paragraphs.en: Moved by his voice, Dorothy asked what she could do to assist him.
paragraphs.zh: 被她声音中的真情所打动，多萝西询问自己能为他做些什么来帮助他。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy returned to the cottage and found an oil-can. She asked anxiously, "Where are your joints?" The Tin Woodman replied, "Oil my neck first."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西回到小木屋里，发现了一瓶油罐。她焦急地问：“你的关节呢？”铁皮人回答说：“先给我润滑油颈吧。”

paragraphs.en: Dorothy complied, gently moving his head until it worked freely. Next, she oiled his arms, carefully bending them back into place.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西依言而行，轻轻转动他的头颅，直到可以自由活动。接着，她为他润滑了双臂，并仔细地将它们重新摆回原位。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman sighed in relief, lowering his axe against the tree. He said, "This is a great comfort; I've been holding this axe for so long. Now oil my legs."
paragraphs.zh: 锡头人松了口气，把斧头靠在树上。他说道：“这真是个好消息；我拿这个斧头已经很久了。现在可以给我的腿涂点油了。”

paragraphs.en: They did so until he could move them freely. The Tin Woodman thanked them repeatedly, appearing polite and grateful.
paragraphs.zh: 他们如此做了，直到他能够自由地活动关节。锡人木偶一再表示感谢，显得礼貌而感激。

paragraphs.en: He then asked, "Why do you wish to see Oz?" Dorothy explained they were on their way to the Emerald City to see the Great Oz. The Tin Woodman inquired if Oz could give him a heart.
paragraphs.zh: 他问道：“你们为什么要见奥兹？”多萝西解释说，她们正前往翡翠城去见伟大的奥兹。接着，铁皮人询问奥兹是否能给他一颗心。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy replied that it would be as easy as giving brains to the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西回答说，这和给稻草人智慧一样容易。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman agreed and proposed joining their party, saying he wanted Oz's help. The Scarecrow readily agreed, and Dorothy was pleased. They set off through the forest until they reached the yellow-brick road leading to the Emerald City.
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人同意了，并提议加入他们的队伍，说他想请奥兹帮忙。稻草人欣然应允，多萝西也很高兴。他们穿过森林前行，直到抵达通向翡翠城的那条黄砖路。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman asked Dorothy to bring an oil-can for his protection against rain. Soon, they encountered a dense forest blocking their path. The Woodman used his axe to clear a way through the trees.
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人请求多萝西带一个油罐，以防雨天使用。不久，他们遇到了一片茂密的森林挡住了去路。铁皮人挥舞着斧头在树木间开辟出一条道路。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was deep in thought and did not notice when the Scarecrow fell into a hole. He called out for help, and Dorothy assisted him back onto the road.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西正陷入沉思，并没有注意到稻草人掉进了一个坑里。他喊道求救，多萝西赶紧把他扶回了路上。

paragraphs.en: "Why didn't you go around the hole?" asked the Tin Woodman.
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么不绕着洞走呢？”铁皮人问道。

paragraphs.en: "I don't know enough," replied the Scarecrow cheerfully. "My head is stuffed with straw, so I'm going to Oz to ask for some brains."
paragraphs.zh: “我还不够了解，”稻草人愉快地回答，“我的脑袋里塞满了稻草，所以我要去奥兹国向她请求一些智慧。”

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman responded, "Brains are not the best things in the world." The Scarecrow then inquired if the Woodman had any.
paragraphs.zh: 铁皮人回答说：“智慧并不是世界上最好的东西。”随后，稻草人询问铁皮人是否还有其他的智慧。

paragraphs.en: "No, my head is empty," answered the Woodman. "But once I had a heart and brains; now, I prefer having a heart."
paragraphs.zh: “不，我的脑袋里空荡荡的，”樵夫回答说，“但我曾经拥有过一颗心和智慧；现在，我宁愿拥有一颗心。”

paragraphs.en: "Why do you say that?" asked the Scarecrow.
paragraphs.zh: “你为什么这么说？”稻草人问道。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman began his story: "I was born to a woodchopper who sold forest wood for a living. After my father's death, I cared for my mother until she passed away. Then, deciding not to live alone, I planned to marry."
paragraphs.zh: 锡头人开始了他的讲述：“我出生在一个伐木工的家庭，他靠卖森林里的木材谋生。在我父亲去世后，我一直照顾母亲直到她离世。随后，决定不独自生活，我打算结婚。”

paragraphs.en: I fell in love with a beautiful Munchkin girl who promised to marry me if I could build her a better house. However, an old woman who lived with her opposed this match, as she wanted the girl to stay and do household chores. The old woman approached the Wicked Witch of the East, who enchanted my axe.
paragraphs.zh: 我爱上了一位美丽的麦琪人女孩，她答应嫁给我，条件是我能为她建造一座更好的房子。然而，与她同住的一位老妇人反对这段婚事，因为她希望女孩留下做家务。这位老妇人去找了东方的恶女巫，恶女巫施魔法使我的斧头失去了效力。

paragraphs.en: One day, while chopping wood eagerly, my axe slipped and cut off my left leg.
paragraphs.zh: 一天，我兴致勃勃地砍木头时，斧头突然滑脱，砍掉了我的左腿。

paragraphs.en: This was a setback, but I went to a tinsmith and had him forge a tin leg that worked well once I got used to it. The Wicked Witch was angered by this, as she had promised the old woman I would not marry the girl. My axe slipped again, cutting off my right leg.
paragraphs.zh: 这虽然有些波折，但我还是找到了一位锡匠，为我打造了一条锡腿。适应了之后，这条腿果然运转良好。然而，恶女巫对此十分不满，因为她曾许诺那位老妇人说我不会娶那个女孩。不幸的是，我的斧头再次失手，这次竟砍掉了我的右腿。

paragraphs.en: Again, I sought the tinsmith for another replacement.
paragraphs.zh: 我又去找了锡匠，希望能再换一副。

paragraphs.en: The enchanted axe then cut off both of my arms. Undeterred, I asked the tinsmith to make tin replacements. Finally, the axe cut off my head, but the tinsmith came just in time and fashioned a new tin head for me.
paragraphs.zh: 魔杖中的魔法斧头随后砍下了我的双臂。我毫不气馁，请求铁匠打造新的铁制手臂。最终，斧头砍下了我的脑袋，但铁匠及时赶到，为我打造了一个新的铁头。

paragraphs.en: The Tin Woodman recounted his ordeal. Initially, he thought he had defeated the Wicked Witch, but she devised a crueler plan. She caused his axe to slip, severing him into two halves.
paragraphs.zh: 锡头人讲述了他所经历的困境。起初，他认为自己已经击败了恶女巫，但女巫另有毒计。她设法让他的斧头脱手，结果将他生生劈成了两半。

paragraphs.en: The tinsmith then crafted a new tin body for him, complete with joints that allowed movement. However, this sacrifice left him heartless, extinguishing his love for the Munchkin maiden.
paragraphs.zh: 随后，锡匠为他打造了一个全新的锡制身躯，并且关节灵活，能够活动。然而，这种牺牲使他的心变得冷酷无情，彻底熄灭了他对芒奇金少女的爱意。

paragraphs.en: Despite his pride in his shiny new body, he feared rusting joints. One day, caught in a rainstorm, he neglected to oil himself, leading to joint failure and leaving him stranded until Dorothy and the Scarecrow rescued him. Reflecting on his life, he realized that losing his heart was his greatest loss.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管他为自己那光鲜的新身体感到骄傲，却害怕关节生锈。一天，他在一场雨中不慎疏忽了自我保养，结果关节失灵，被困在那里，直到多萝西和稻草人前来救援。回想起自己的人生，他意识到失去内心的温暖才是最大的遗憾。

paragraphs.en: He yearned for Oz to grant him a new one, promising to return to the Munchkin maiden.
paragraphs.zh: 他渴望奥兹能够给他一个新的心，承诺要回到麦当琪的少女身边。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy and the Scarecrow listened intently to the Tin Woodman's tale. The Scarecrow expressed his desire for brains instead of a heart, believing that happiness comes from wisdom rather than emotion. The Tin Woodman, however, chose the heart, valuing happiness over intelligence.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西和稻草人全神贯注地聆听着铁皮人讲述的故事。稻草人表达了自己渴望拥有一颗智慧之心，而非情感之心，认为幸福源自智慧而非情感。然而，铁皮人选择了心脏，他更看重幸福胜过智慧。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy remained silent, unsure if her friends were correct about their needs. She decided that as long as they returned to Kansas and Aunt Em, it didn't matter whether the Tin Woodman lacked brains or the Scarecrow a heart.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西沉默不语，不确定朋友们是否正确地认识到了自己的需求。她决定，只要他们能回到堪萨斯和艾玛婶婶身边，铁皮人缺少智慧或稻草人缺少心脏就无关紧要了。

paragraphs.en: What troubled her most was the nearly empty bread basket. Another meal for herself and Toto would leave them with nothing. Neither the Tin Woodman nor the Scarecrow ate, but Dorothy needed food to survive.
paragraphs.zh: 让她最为担忧的是几乎空荡的面包篮。再为她自己和托托准备一餐，他们就将一无所有了。虽然铁皮人和稻草人都不吃东西，但多萝西却需要食物来维持生命。
